title: Display and manage transactions in core financial application

story.so_that: I can track my financial activity and maintain an accurate account balance
story.i_want: view my transactions, add new transactions, and see my current balance in a secure banking application

journey.before: User logs into their banking account with mock credentials
journey.during: User views their transaction history, adds new transactions, and monitors their account balance
journey.after: User logs out with confidence that their transactions are recorded and balance is accurate

capability_breakdown.core_action: Display transactions for logged-in account, add new transactions, and maintain accurate running balance
inputs: Transaction date (today or past dates only)
outputs: List of transactions filtered by account (up to 50-100 displayed, system handles 5,000-10,000)
state_changes: Account balance updated when transaction is added
New transaction persisted to transaction log

ui: Login screen with account selection and password input
Transaction list view with date, payee, amount columns
Add transaction form with date picker, payee input, amount input
Error message display for validation failures
api: POST /api/auth/login - authenticate user with mock credentials
database: Transactions table (id, account_id, date, payee, amount, created_at)
external_services: Python analytics sidecar for transaction data analysis

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Display existing transactions for logged-in account
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a user is logged in When they view the transaction list Then they see all transactions impacting their account sorted by date descending

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add new transactions to existing accounts
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a user is logged in When they submit a new transaction with valid date, payee, and amount Then the transaction is recorded and balance is updated immediately

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Show only transactions that impact the current user's account
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given multiple accounts exist in the system When a user logs in Then they see only transactions where their account is involved
Given transactions are displayed When a user views the balance Then it reflects the sum of all transactions for their account

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cannot create transactions for more money than available
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an account has a balance of $100 When a user attempts to add a transaction of -$150 Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Insufficient funds'

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Can only set transactions for today or past dates
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a user is adding a transaction When they attempt to set a date in the future Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Future dates not allowed'
Given a transaction exists in the list When a user views the transaction Then no delete button or option is available

acceptance_criteria.criterion: System handles up to 50-100 transactions displayed at once
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an account has 100 transactions When the user views the transaction list Then all 100 are displayed without pagination and load time is under 2 seconds

acceptance_criteria.criterion: System handles 5,000-10,000 transactions in common transaction log
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the system contains 10,000 transactions across all accounts When queries are executed Then response time is under 3 seconds
Given 5 accounts exist (A-E) When a user logs in with Account B credentials Then they access Account B and see only Account B transactions

acceptance_criteria.criterion: User session persists across page refreshes
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a user is logged in When they refresh the page Then they remain logged in and see their transactions
Given a user is logged in When they click logout Then their session ends and they return to login screen

edge_cases.gherkin: Given a user is adding a transaction When they leave payee field empty Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Payee is required'
Given a user is adding a transaction When they enter amount as 0 Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Amount must be non-zero'
Given a user is adding a transaction When they enter amount exceeding $1,000,000 Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Amount exceeds maximum'
Given a user is adding a transaction When they enter payee with special characters (e.g., 'Café René') Then the transaction is accepted and displays correctly
Given a user is adding a transaction When they enter payee name exceeding 500 characters Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Payee name too long'
Given a new account with zero transactions When a user logs in Then they see empty transaction list with message 'No transactions yet'
Given an account has zero balance When a user attempts to add a negative transaction Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Insufficient funds'

edge_cases.criterion: Multiple users accessing same account simultaneously
edge_cases.gherkin: Given two users are logged into the same account When one adds a transaction Then the other sees the updated balance after refresh
Given a user is adding a transaction When they enter an invalid date format Then the transaction is rejected with error 'Invalid date format'

edge_cases.criterion: Database connection failure during transaction creation
edge_cases.gherkin: Given database is unavailable When a user attempts to add a transaction Then error message 'Service temporarily unavailable' is displayed
Given a user session has expired When they attempt to add a transaction Then they are redirected to login with message 'Session expired'
Given a user enters incorrect password When they attempt to login Then error message 'Invalid credentials' is displayed

open_questions.question: What is the maximum length for payee name?
What is the maximum transaction amount allowed?
How should the system handle decimal precision for amounts (2 decimal places, more)?
Should the running balance be calculated in real-time or cached?
What happens when a transaction would result in negative balance? Hard reject or allow with warning?
Should transactions be sorted by date ascending or descending by default?
How long should user sessions last before expiring?
Should the system support multiple currencies or single currency only?
What date format should be used for display (MM/DD/YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, ISO)?
Should the mock data generation utility be part of the application or separate tool?
How should the Python analytics sidecar integrate with the main application?
What analytics capabilities are needed from the Python sidecar in the core app?

new_code: React frontend application with routing and state management
.NET Web API with controllers for auth, accounts, and transactions
SQL database schema for accounts and transactions

recommendation.approach: Build this as the foundational core application first, as all other features depend on it. Implement in phases: (1) Authentication and account isolation, (2) Transaction display with filtering, (3) Transaction creation with validation, (4) Balance calculation and display. Use TDD approach with comprehensive test coverage for business rules.
risks: Balance calculation errors could cause data integrity issues - mitigate with extensive unit tests and validation
Concurrent transaction creation could lead to race conditions - implement proper transaction isolation in database
Performance degradation with large transaction volumes - ensure proper database indexing and query optimization
Session management complexity - use established session libraries rather than custom implementation
alternatives_considered: Single-page application vs multi-page: Chose SPA (React) for better user experience and state management
Real-time balance calculation vs cached: Recommend real-time calculation for accuracy, with caching as optimization if needed
Mock authentication vs real auth: Mock is sufficient for benchmark purposes and reduces complexity
next_steps: Clarify open questions with stakeholders (decimal precision, max amounts, date formats)
Create database schema and migration scripts
Set up project structure for React frontend and .NET backend
Implement mock data generation utility for testing
Begin TDD cycle starting with authentication tests
